user.title: Add an HA Watcher
user.description:
This creates a private web address (a webhook) that your ha-watcher service sends its status to. The ha-watcher service must run on a different machine from Home Assistant. You will see the address after you press Submit.

A random shared secret is filled in below. Keep it: with it, only reports signed by your watcher are accepted, so nobody who sees or guesses the address can fake an "all OK" report.

data.name: Name
data.local_only: Only accept reports from the local network

data_description.name: Shown as the device name, for example the name of the machine running ha-watcher.
data_description.local_only: Recommended. Turn off only if the watcher reaches Home Assistant over the internet; a shared secret is then required. Behind a reverse proxy or tunnel on your network, every request can look local, so this setting may not protect you there: keep the shared secret.
data_description.shared_secret: At least 16 characters. Put the same secret in the watcher's `home_assistant_push.secret` setting; it is shown again after you press Submit. Clear the field to accept unsigned reports (local network only; not recommended).

create_entry.default:
Copy this address into the `home_assistant_push.url` setting of your ha-watcher service:

`{webhook_url}`

Keep it private: anyone who knows it can send status reports. Reports are not signed. Setting a shared secret under this integration's **Configure** button is strongly recommended; Home Assistant shows a repair until one is set.
create_entry.signed:
Copy this address into the `home_assistant_push.url` setting of your ha-watcher service:

`{webhook_url}`

and this shared secret into its `home_assistant_push.secret` setting:

`{shared_secret}`

Keep both private. Until the watcher uses the same secret its reports are refused. You can see the address again, and change the secret, under this integration's **Configure** button.

error.secret_too_short: The shared secret must be at least 16 characters long.
error.secret_required: A shared secret is required when reports are accepted from outside the local network.

init.title: HA Watcher options
init.description:
Webhook address for the ha-watcher service:

`{webhook_url}`

Keep it private. Home Assistant's own log can contain this address; remove it before posting logs anywhere.

Shared secret: at least {min_secret_len} characters, strongly recommended and required when reports are accepted from outside the local network. A random one you can use: `{suggested_secret}`

data.local_only: Only accept reports from the local network

data_description.offline_timeout: Mark the watcher offline when no valid report has arrived for this many minutes. Use at least twice the watcher's report interval.
data_description.local_only: Turn off only if the watcher reaches Home Assistant over the internet; a shared secret is then required. Behind a reverse proxy or tunnel on your network, every request can look local, so this setting may not protect you there: set a shared secret.
data_description.shared_secret: When set, only reports signed with this secret are accepted. Put the same secret in the watcher's `home_assistant_push.secret` setting. Leave empty to turn signing off (local network only; not recommended).

error.secret_too_short: The shared secret must be at least 16 characters long.
error.secret_required: A shared secret is required when reports are accepted from outside the local network.

no_shared_secret.title: {name}: status reports are not signed
no_shared_secret.description:
The HA Watcher entry **{name}** accepts status reports without a shared secret. Anyone on your network who sees one report, or learns the webhook address, can send fake "all OK" reports and hide a watcher that has stopped. Behind a reverse proxy or tunnel, outside requests can also look local.

To fix this, open the integration's **Configure** dialog, set a shared secret (a random one is suggested there), and put the same secret in the watcher's `home_assistant_push.secret` setting. Until the watcher uses it, its reports are refused, so update both together.

no_shared_secret_remote.title: {name}: unsigned reports accepted from the internet
no_shared_secret_remote.description:
The HA Watcher entry **{name}** accepts status reports from outside the local network without a shared secret. Anyone who learns the webhook address can send fake "all OK" reports from anywhere and hide a watcher that has stopped.

To fix this, open the integration's **Configure** dialog, set a shared secret (a random one is suggested there), and put the same secret in the watcher's `home_assistant_push.secret` setting. Until the watcher uses it, its reports are refused, so update both together.
